brief.briefing:
Risk this week
Elevated and well above normal for this time of year. About 28% chance of flash drought starting this week, compared to 4% normally — about 7.1 times normal. About 44% chance in the next 28 days vs 13% normally. Most weeks with elevated risk do not end in flash drought, but stay alert.

Why
Topsoil is okay now. Root-zone moisture near 64th percentile, 0% of local area already in drought, Drought Monitor shows none. Deeper soil is drier, near 37th percentile. Forecast drives risk: rainfall well below normal over the next couple weeks, temperature above normal, air dryness far above normal. 83% of forecast scenarios show a hot, dry spell. You sit among the highest-risk blocks in the region.

What to watch
Rain totals this week and next, heat and drying winds, and how fast surface moisture drops.

Suggested actions
Check soil moisture often, delay non-essential tillage, have irrigation ready if you have it, and avoid stressing young crops. Review feed and water plans.

example.draft:
The Midwest was mostly dry this week, with only a few tenths of an inch of precipitation measured across the region. The dryness has led to some expansion of D0 and D1 in central and southern Illinois, and D0 in northern Illinois. The rest of the region remains unchanged this week.

High Plains
The High Plains were also dry this week, with only a few tenths of an inch of precipitation measured across the region. The dryness has led to some expansion of D1 in eastern Nebraska and D1 and D2 in North Dakota. The rest of the region remains unchanged this week.
example.real:
Midwest
On this week’s map, some minor expansion of areas of Moderate Drought (D1) occurred in central Illinois in response to short-term precipitation deficits (60 day to 6 months), low streamflows, and areas of below-normal soil moisture. Overall, the region was generally dry during the past week with below-normal average temperatures in the southern half of the region and above-normal temperatures in the northern portion with the greatest positive anomalies (6 to 12+ degrees F) observed in western Minnesota. According to the NOAA NOHRSC, 13% of the Northern Great Lakes region was covered by snow with an average snow depth of 0.2 inches and a maximum depth of 5.4 inches.

High Plains
On this week’s map, areas of the region—including southwestern North Dakota and central Nebraska—saw modest expansion in areas of Severe Drought (D2) as well as expansion in areas of Moderate Drought (D1) in southwestern North Dakota in response to a combination of factors—short-term precipitation deficits, lack of seasonal snow cover, depleted soil moisture, and unseasonably warm temperatures (12 to 20 degrees F above normal)—during the past week. In the eastern Plains of Colorado, areas of Extreme Drought (D3) and Exceptional Drought (D4) expanded where long-term precipitation deficits continued to mount.

ask.q: Do I need to start my pivot today?
ask.answer:
Not today. Wait for the next forecast in 2 days.

Your chance of a flash drought in the next 7 days is 12%, about 4 times normal - normal is 3%. Starting your pivot today is worth about $2 an acre, waiting is worth about $2 an acre too.

Your soil is 52% full, about 3 inches low, with about 1 day until stress if no rain. So you are getting dry, but the forecast does not yet say to run full time.

ask.q: I put an inch on yesterday. Do I still need to start?
ask.answer:
Got your inch from yesterday logged.

Your soil water is 66% full, about 2 inches short, about 4 days until stress if no rain.

Flash drought chance is 12% in the next 7 days, that's 4 times the normal 3%, and 7% the week after. Forecasts are uncertain and can change fast.

Advice is not yet - wait for the next forecast in 2 days.

Starting extra today is worth about $2 an acre, waiting for the next forecast is also about $2 an acre. If it does come, having 7 days warning can save about $77 an acre.

ask.q: What's the chance of a flash drought in the next two weeks, and is that unusual for this time of year?
ask.answer:
For your farm, chance of flash drought next week is about 12%. Chance the week after is about 7%.

Normal for this time of year is about 3%, so next week is about 4 times normal. That is unusual and forecasts can shift.
